title: Carrick Confirms a Staggering Nine Man Utd Players to Miss Critical Como Clash
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell6:00 PM EDTMichael Carrick has an injury crisis to navigate. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesManchester United will be severely shorthanded when they take on Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

The Red Devils come into the European bout desperate to snap a dreadful six-game winless run. Michael Carrick’s men have not collected three points since their 4–0 victory over Sabah in their Champions League opener back on Sept. 10.

A win in Italy would raise the spirits at United, but getting past Como will be anything but easy for a team stuck in such a rut. Cesc Fàbregas’s young and exciting squad has a knack for pulling off magical moments, and a Champions League night against one of the biggest clubs in the world is the perfect stage to make a statement.
A devastating injury crisis is also working against United. Carrick gave updates on his sidelined players ahead of the clash, and it was bad news after bad news.

Leny Yoro (center) is suspended for the clash. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesSuspension: One GameUCL Return Date: Nov. 3 vs. RomaBefore we get into all the players stuck in the infirmary, let’s get the obvious out of the way: Leny Yoro is unavailable against Como. The center back was sent off in the team’s 2–0 defeat to Atlético Madrid last time out and is therefore suspended for Wednesday’s match.
Once he serves his one-game ban, Yoro will be free to feature in the Red Devils’ next Champions League clash against Roma on Nov. 3.

Lisandro Martínez is a big loss for United. / Michael Steele/Getty ImagesInjury: ThighPotential Return Date: Oct. 25 vs. BournemouthOne week ago, Lisandro Martínez was going on a tirade after United’s defeat to Atlético Madrid. Now, he will not even be present in Italy to play or comment on the team’s next European bout.

Martínez, who escaped with just a fine for his explosive rant, only lasted 45 minutes against Leeds United at the weekend. Carrick revealed the Argentine suffered a thigh injury, one that is keeping him in Manchester midweek.
“Licha [Martínez] is not too bad, but he is not with us,” Carrick confirmed on Tuesday. “We will have to see if he’s ready for the weekend or not.”

Marcus Rashford remains unfit. / Angel Martinez/Getty ImagesInjury: HipPotential Return Date: UnknownMarcus Rashford’s return to Manchester United hasn’t exactly gone to plan. The England international does not have a single goal contribution in eight appearances and is dealing with a lingering hip issue from the 2026 World Cup.
He was an unused substitute at the weekend against Leeds and is expected to miss out again against Como.

“Marcus is still feeling a little bit of a hip issue that we are trying to overcome,” Carrick revealed in his pregame press conference. The manager did not specify a recovery timeline for the forward.

Kobbie Mainoo is dealing with an unspecified problem.  / Alex Livesey/Getty ImagesInjury: UndisclosedPotential Return Date: Oct. 31 vs. ChelseaThere’s a lot more uncertainty to what’s keeping Kobbie Mainoo sidelined. United have not been forthcoming with his specific injury, but the problem has kept the midfielder out for the team’s last two games, a trend that will continue.
“Kobbie, maybe 10 days or so but that’s not exact,” Carrick said on Tuesday, referring to how much longer the England international will be sidelined.
Should Mainoo recover relatively on schedule, he could be ready in time to face off with Chelsea at the end of the month.

Luke Shaw’s fitness woes are back. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesInjury: UndisclosedPotential Return Date: NovemberIt’s a pretty surefire bet to always expect Luke Shaw to feature on these types of lists. The fullback is as injury-prone as they come, and unsurprisingly returned to the infirmary after just one appearance following the September-October international break.

Shaw’s injury is undisclosed by United. Carrick also did not give a specific recovery timeline; instead, he just said the left back will be out a “little bit longer” than Mainoo, hinting a return in November at the earliest.

Ayden Heaven is still recovering from sickness. / Molly Darlington/Getty ImagesInjury: SicknessPotential Return Date: Oct. 25 vs. BournemouthAdding to United’s defensive woes is Ayden Heaven’s sickness. The center back missed out at the weekend due to the illness and has yet to recover.
Carrick confirmed the bug is keeping Heaven at home midweek. The good news is Heaven should be ready to feature against Bournemouth on Sunday.
